'When this defends, reveal the top card of your deck. If it's an Evo, put it on top of your deck. Otherwise, put it on the bottom.' Mechanologist Block (BrightLights).

TRIGGER: TRIGGERED + ON_DEFEND, the spelling shipped defending equipment uses (evo/torque_tuned_red.json carries two ON_DEFEND abilities; sea/helmsmans_peak, hvy/apex_bonebreaker et al.). ON_DEFEND is wired in engine._setup_dsl_listeners and reaches the cards that declared as defenders, so 'when this defends' fires on this card's own defence.

SHAPE copied from .drafts/bone_vizier.json, whose printed text is the same reveal-then-branch sentence ('reveal the top card of your deck. If ..., put it on top of your deck. Otherwise, put it on the bottom.') with only the test differing.

REVEAL: REVEAL_TOP_DECK (effect_types.py:2229-2256, read this session) reads amount/into, marks the top card is_public (a real public reveal), and stores it as a LIST under ref 'revealed'. It hard-codes the CONTROLLER's own deck (:2243-2244), which is 'your deck'. Without 'into' the handler stores nothing and both branches would have nothing to test or move - the failure mode recorded for berserk_yellow in .review.

BRANCH: CONDITIONAL_EFFECT reads when/then/else (effect_types.py:3697+); 'when', NOT 'conditions' - the loader pops the latter as an effect-level gate and would skip the else branch entirely. The test is REF_IS_TYPE (condition_types.py:2011-2043, read this session): it reads 'types'/'card_types' (or the singular spellings), unions the ref card's types AND subtypes, and unwraps a one-element list - which is what REVEAL_TOP_DECK always stores for amount 1.

'EVO' IS A SUBTYPE: Evo cards carry subtypes ['Evo', ...] in card data (evo/evo_work_queue.json entries), and the shipped corpus already filters on it - evo/heavy_artillery_red.json counts Evos via COUNT_PERMANENT subtype 'Evo', evo/demolition_protocol_red.json via an object-target filter, evo/war_machine_red.json via token_type 'Evo'. REF_IS_TYPE's types+subtypes union therefore matches 'it's an Evo' exactly.

PLACEMENT: PUT_REF_TOP / PUT_REF_BOTTOM (effect_types.py:3614-3639, read this session) read 'ref' and default player OWNER - the revealed card's owner is Firewall's controller, so the default is correct and needs no override.

Edge cases fail closed: an empty deck stores [], REF_IS_TYPE finds no target and answers False, and PUT_REF_BOTTOM returns early on an empty ref - no crash, no move. PUT_REF_TOP on a card still sitting on top of the deck is the printed no-op ('put it on top'); the reveal never moved it.
